chunks: As for what al-Ḥusayn ibn Saʿīd narrated from Ṣafwān, from Isḥāq ibn ʿAmmār, who said:

I said to Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام: A menstruating woman sweats in her garment. He said: She should wash it. I said: Then if beneath the shift there is a waist-wrapper, and the sweat only reaches what is beneath the waist-wrapper? He said: She should not wash it.

Thus, the proper way regarding this report is that we interpret it to mean when there is some najasah there, because in the case of a menstruating woman, what is beneath the waist-wrapper generally does not remain free of najasah. For that reason, washing the garment becomes obligatory upon her. This indicates that.
ai.seo_question: Does the sweat of a menstruating woman make clothing impure and require washing?
ai.summary: This hadith addresses the ruling on the sweat of a menstruating woman when it affects clothing. The report distinguishes between circumstances in which the garment is likely affected by najasah and circumstances in which the sweat reaches only an area protected by a waist-wrapper, indicating a jurisprudential consideration of ritual purity.
